Specifications for the procurement of the Equipment SPECT/CT Scanne r (Gamma Camera) for the Department of Nuclear Medicine, JIPMER, Puducherry 605006 Equipment: SPECT/CT Scanner (Gamma Camera) - 01 no. The following are specifications as approved by the committee at the specification vetting committee meeting after incorporation of the pre-bid meeting held subsequently on August 3, 2026. The specification s have been approved by the competent authority. A Technical Specification Item Name: SPECT/CT Scanner (Gamma Camera) Supply and installation of latest technology dual-headed variable angle SPECT/CT with at least 16 or mo re slices CT, with advanced workstations, and buy-back of existing SPECT-CT. International installation a s a benchmark may be accepted. Scope of the work: 1 The primary vendor will be responsible for the complete turnkey work/supply, installation, and commissioning of the new gamma camera and entire decommissioning process of the old gam ma camera as per AERB guidelines. 2 Cost of the civil/electrical work for renovation of the camera room including air-conditioning, til ing, flooring, painting, false-roofing of the console, post-injection waiting room, dose administr ation room, toilets, radiopharmacy area, waiting areas, corridors, TMT room, reporting room, a nd other rooms as necessary, should be quoted separately. Air-conditioning should be provide d in the camera room through suitable mechanisms such as AHU or VRV in two sets that woul d operate alternatively for 12 hours in a day. The vendor has to ensure that optimum working temperature and humidity are maintained throughout the day in the camera room. Air-conditi oning for the gamma camera room, console room, and reporting room to be provided as follow s: a. Ductable air conditioning with humidity control b. Vendors shall visit the site and decide the suitable type, design, number, and characteristics of air-conditioning and dehumidification, such that the recommended temperature and humidi ty are maintained. c. Two sets of air-conditioning should be provided for the gamma camera room to operate every 12 hours alternately. d. The existing AHU connection of the hospital to be disconnected during normal use with an op tion to enable its operation when both the sets of air-conditioning fail in extreme situations. 3 The radiation equipment provided for this tender must comply with prescribed international an d national radiation safety standards and norms. An AERB type approval certificate or NOC mu st be included.

4 The final price comparison for award of the contract will be based on the price of the gamma c amera, accessories, turnkey, and CAMC and after deducting the price offered for the old camer a. Vendors should visit the department for inspection of the old equipment as well as space av ailable for the installation of the new SPECT/CT system. A certificate should be attached that t he space is adequate for the installation of the quoted system. 5 All quality assurance and acceptance tests in accordance with NEMA and AERB standards mus t be conducted by the company engineer in the presence of the department’s Nuclear Medicin e radiological safety officer or technologist. These results will be forwarded to AERB to obtain t he operational license for the equipment. 6 The bidder should quote the price for buy-back of the old SPECT/CT (Siemens Symbia T6). A re ceipt will be provided by the vendor in return for invoice given by JIPMER for the buyback equi pment. The buyback option has been selected on GeM portal and the approved process on the GeM portal for buyback option will be followed. The following are the items offered for buybac k: Gamma camera (SPECT/CT), LEHR and HEGP collimators, collimator cart, acquisition station, and UPS/inverter of the system. Leaded glass and processing workstation are not included. 7 The tenders along with all the commitments, claims, specifications, guarantee, warrantee etc. pertaining to the equipment shall be submitted directly by the Manufacturer/Principals (also r eferred to as Vendors or Suppliers) who shall be wholly and solely responsible for all the state ments/commitments in this connection. 8 Any options or added facilities not indicated in the specifications may also be given. Any impr oved modifications or updated versions of the system can be included in the quotation. 9 Inland LC will be created after selection of the successful bidder. Payment Term: Inland Letter of Credit will be established for 100% order value, 80% payme nt shall be m ade by us, against the presentation of original Shipping documents. Balance 20 % will be released after co mpletion of satisfactory installation and commissioning of the whol e system and upon receipt of Bank Guar antee for 3% of total Order value towards performanc e security to be valid for till warranty period from the date of installation. LC Payment will be d one offline and updated through bulk update on GeM. The maximum duration for delivery of equipment allowed is 180 days from the date of opening of LC and maximum duration for installation is 35 days. I General 1 The SPECT/CT equipment with CT detectors that can generate 16 or more CT slices quoted sh ould be the top-of-the-line model offered by the manufacturer, fully compliant with the technic al specifications. 2 The system should be capable of performing all Planar, Dynamic, SPECT, Gated Cardiac SPECT , whole body SPECT, and Whole Body imaging applications. 3 The system should be capable of performing fast-rotation high-resolution CT image-based atte nuation correction on the same patient table for nuclear medicine images, as well as functiona l-anatomical image fusion. The system should be able to perform CT imaging of the whole bod y along with whole body SPECT. 4 The system should include an integrated CT hardware option for transmission attenuation corr ection and functional-anatomical image fusion.

5 The system should be supplied with both image fusion software and hardware. 6 The vendor should provide copies of all Application, Operating, and Service manuals in duplica te at the time of machine handover. At least one set of these manuals should be provided in a computer-readable format. 7 Details for insurance for the equipment is enclosed in annexure I. II Gantry 1 The gantry should be wide open with capabilities for clockwise and anticlockwise movements. 2 It must support variable angle configurations, including 90° and 180° detector arrangements f or SPECT, as well as horizontal and vertical upright positions for static views. 3 The design should include a 70 cm bore size and a 50 cm CT Scan FOV to accommodate large patients. 4 Emergency stop buttons should be integrated into the gantry. 5 Gantry motion must be controlled via a remote control handset and user-defined programs. 6 A persistence scope (LCD color display) should be mounted on the gantry or wall to continuou sly show patient position and gantry parameters. III Detectors 1 Detectors should have a large field of view with a rectangular field of view design with best po ssible UFOV of at least 500 x 350 mm (± 5%) to ensure comprehensive patient breadth cover age. 2 The crystal thickness should be 9.5 mm (3/8”). 3 The number of photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) should be 59 or more per detector with 1 ADC per PMT (True digital detector). 4 The detectors should be equipped with automatic body countering (ABC). 5 The system should include facilities for automatic correction of energy, linearity, and uniformit y. 6 Performance parameters must conform to the latest NEMA NU 1 standards applicable at the ti me of equipment supply, with supporting literature. 7 Maximum intrinsic count rate > 300 kcps for each detector. 8 Intrinsic energy resolution (Tc-99m@20 kcps, FWHM) equal or less than 9.5%.

9 Intrinsic Flood uniformity: i. Differential: UFOV<=3% and CFOV<=2.5% ii. Integral: UFOV<=4% and CFOV<=3% 10 Intrinsic Spatial resolution i. FWHM of UFOV < or = 3.8 to 4.1 mm ii. FWHM of CFOV < or = 3.7 to 7.8 mm 11 System Spatial sensitivity using LEHR Collimator at 10 cm for CFOV better than 200 cpm/micr oCurie of Tc-99m in 20% energy window (10% on either side of the photopeak). IV CT Specifications 1 The system should be enabled with a fast rotation CT scanner with full rotation capable of gen erating at least 16 slices or more per rotation. 2 The system must generate attenuation correction maps for application to nuclear medicine im ages, enabling precise body attenuation correction and accurate localization through the fusio n of SPECT and CT images. 3 The system should incorporate the latest ultra-low dose technology for attenuation correction, specifically designed to minimize radiation exposure for follow-up and cardiac patients. The sy stem should also be able to generate diagnostic quality CT images. 4 Patient port aperture: 70 cm 5 Transaxial field of view should be ≥ 50 cm 6 Continuous generator to support sustained and continuous X-ray generation. 7 Tube current: 30-200 mA or better 8 KV range should be from 80-130 kV or better 9 Anode heat storage capacity: 2 MHU or better 10 Pitch factor (volume pitch) should be variable between 0.5 to 1.5 or better and should be user selectable without affecting SFOV of at least 50 cm. 11 Scan time for a complete 360 degree scan should be 1 sec or less.

12 High contrast resolution should be ≥ 15 lp / cm @ 0 or 1% MTF. Low contrast resolution should be ≤ 5 mm at 3 HV(0.3%) with 20 cm CATPHAN Phantom 13 The slice thickness of the CT-reconstructed image should be 0.625 mm or better 14 The system should feature an inbuilt laser light system designed to control and ensure the iso- centric positioning of the patient in all planes. 15 The system should include filters, collimators, and other specialized features designed to mini mize radiation dose to the patient. 16 The system should specify the focal spot size and number in compliance with IEC recommend ations. 17 The system should support automatic selection of focal spots in accordance with IEC recomme ndations. V Collimators 1 The system should include high-precision collimators equipped with collision sensors for safety and storage carts for easy collimator changes. i. Low Energy High Resolution (LEHR) – One Pair ii. High Energy General Purpose – One Pair iii. Medium energy general purpose – One Pair Patient Table VI 1 Should have a single universal table for all studies i.e., Planar, SPECT, Whole body imaging and CT images. 2 The tabletop should be made of low attenuation material, preferably carbon fiber, with attenu ation not exceeding 10% at 140 keV. It should be covered with a mattress pad and equipped with straps for patient support. Head support, hand support, and calf support should be provid ed. An additional flat panel bed for radiotherapy planning should be provided as part of the sta ndard equipment. 3 Table should be able to withstand at least 200 Kg of body weight. 4 Whole body imaging covering should not be less than 180 cm. 5 Should have automated interactive scale at bedside for faster patient positioning. 6 The table should move to the home position on a single command.

7 The table should be equipped with a height-adjustment feature to facilitate easy patient transf er. It should be movable to accommodate imaging for sitting, standing, and stretcher/wheelch air patients, with a lower range of vertical motion of 24 inches or less. 8 The system should come with a paediatric pallet, adjustable head positioning pallets, and arm rests for injection and cardiac procedures. 9 The system should also include leg support and Velcro straps for patient restraint and support. Head extender for brain imaging should be provided. VII Acquisition Workstation 1 One Acquisition station independent of the main processing unit capable of data acquisition in static, dynamic, multi-gated, whole body scanning, SPECT and Gated SPECT. 2 High performance PC of latest specifications with multi-tasking operating system, compatible mother board and integrated graphic card. It should have a minimum of 16 GB RAM or more, 2.5 GHz or more processor speed, 1 TB hard disk or more as SSD. High resolution (1024 x 102 4 or more) antiglare flat panel square LED monitor of minimum 17” size or more. It should also have a CD and DVD combo drive with a writer facility. 3 Fully integrated CT system capable of acquiring X-ray transmission data along with nuclear e mission data. SPECT & CT data acquisition should be on the same console. 4 Image acquisition and data display should be from 64 x 64 matrix up to 256 x 1024 matrix. 5 Acquisition termination by preset time, preset count with ability to manually pause, resume a nd stop all types of acquisitions. 6 Pre-defined acquisition protocols as well as facility for users to configure customized protocols . 7 Should have zoom, pan, and rotate features. 8 Should have on line live display of acquired data and imaging parameters during acquisition 9 Should have cinematic display of dynamic, MUGA & all multi frame studies. 10 Should provide system compatible ECG Gating Device with all leads and cables for MUGA / Gat ed Data acquisition. There should be ECG and R-to-R Histogram display during acquisition. It s hould indicate frames per R-R interval and maximum frame rate capability. The device and De tachable leads should be integrated with the table. Two sets of cables and leads should be pro vided. 11 Acquisition software should include camera quality control activities including Centre of rotatio n (COR) correction, Uniformity correction maps, Energy, Sensitivity and Linearity maps, Daily / Weekly QC including Gantry calibration, Energy spectrum histogram (PHA) display, QC for Wh ole Body Acquisition, QC for Balancing sensitivity of both Detector heads.
